headline: Telechat adds mobile approvals for Claude AI's destructive CLI commands
summary: Telechat's Desktop Bridge now allows developers to remotely approve or deny Claude AI's critical commands directly from their phone via popular messaging apps, preventing workflow blocks.
details: Telechat, a self-hosted Claude AI bot, has introduced a Desktop Bridge feature with mobile approvals, enhancing devops workflows. This allows developers to manage Claude's actions remotely.

Previously, AI agents like Claude Code would halt and wait for human input when a destructive command or approval checkpoint was reached, causing delays if the developer was away from their workstation.
The new Desktop Bridge connects the Claude Code session to a developer's phone via Telegram, WhatsApp, or Slack. When Claude requires approval, the request is sent to the messaging app.

This enables use cases such as unattended CI/CD with a human gate, allowing pipelines to continue without blocking. It also facilitates overnight tasks, letting developers approve decisions from their phone in the morning without context loss.
Developers can also use it for mobile pair programming, reviewing and approving Claude's work between meetings, or adding context via chat.
Telechat runs locally, intercepting Claude's approval prompts, formatting them, and sending them to the configured messaging app. The response from the phone then flows back to unblock the AI agent.

headline_marked: [[DeepSeek-V4-Flash API now in public beta]], offering V4-Pro & V4-Flash via OpenAI & Anthropic interfaces
headline: DeepSeek-V4-Flash API now in public beta, offering V4-Pro & V4-Flash via OpenAI & Anthropic interfaces
summary: DeepSeek's latest models, V4-Pro and V4-Flash, are now accessible through both OpenAI and Anthropic interfaces. Legacy API model names will be discontinued in three months.
details: The DeepSeek-V4-Flash API is officially in public beta, allowing users to access it by setting the model name to deepseek-v4-flash. This update makes the latest models available through a consistent API calling method.

The DeepSeek API now supports both V4-Pro and V4-Flash, accessible via both the OpenAI ChatCompletions interface and the Anthropic interface. The base_url for API access remains unchanged for these new models.

Legacy API model names, deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner, will be discontinued on July 24, 2026. During the three-month transition period, these names will point to the non-thinking and thinking modes of deepseek-v4-flash.

Previous iterations saw significant advancements, including DeepSeek-Coder-V2-0614 reaching GPT-4-Turbo-0409 levels in coding capabilities. The deepseek-chat model also improved instruction following, with IFEval accuracy jumping from 63.9% to 77.6%.

DeepSeek has also implemented innovative hard disk caching, which has resulted in a further order of magnitude reduction in API prices. This makes their advanced models more cost-effective for developers.
